Name: Sagrada Família
Cost Range: 26 EUR basic / 24 EUR under-30 / 36 EUR with tower (under 11 free, still needs QR)
Tips: BOOKED: Thu 27 Aug 2026, entry 17:45, English guided tour 18:30, code 103719876. Nominative ticket — bring passports, names are checked. Be at the Carrer de la Marina entrance by 17:30; 15-min window enforced. Evening slot means western Passion-facade light: nave glows red and gold. FREE SECOND VISIT: International Mass Sundays 09:00 (also Saturdays 20:00) — no ticket, no booking, capacity limited so queue from 08:15. Enter at the Nativity facade on Carrer de la Marina. Morning light through the Nativity side is blue-green — the opposite of the paid evening slot.

Name: Park Güell
Cost Range: 18 EUR monumental zone (7-12: 13.50 EUR; under 7 free; outer park free)
Tips: BOOKED: Thu 27 Aug 2026, 09:30, 4 general tickets, 72 EUR paid, locator 700328431455. 30-min entry window from 09:30 and no re-entry once you exit. Dragon Staircase + 86-column Hypostyle Hall are must-sees. Free outer park has great city views.
Family: Good — older kids and teens love it

Name: Casa Batlló
Tips: Book ahead. Rooftop dragon-spine tiles and bone-column main salon are extraordinary. Magic Nights evening option available. On the Manzana de la Discordia block.

Name: Casa Milà (La Pedrera)
Tips: Book ahead. The rooftop warrior chimneys are the attraction. Go late afternoon for best light. Evening concert La Pedrera de Nit is expensive but magical.

Name: Hospital de Sant Pau
Address: C/ de Sant Antoni Maria Claret 167 Eixample
Cost Range: 18 EUR before 14:00 / 17 EUR after; ages 12-24 12.60/11.90 EUR; under 12 free (verified 2026)
Tips: World's largest Art Nouveau complex. Almost no queues in August. Daily 09:30-18:30, last entry 18:00. Our slot: Day 2 15:45 after siesta (~57.80 EUR for four at the pm rate). Ten-minute walk down pedestrian Avinguda de Gaudi straight to the Sagrada Familia. UNESCO World Heritage.

Name: Barcelona Cathedral
Address: Pla de la Seu s/n El Gòtic
Cost Range: 16 EUR cultural visit (students up to 25: 14 EUR); ~19 EUR tier adds rooftop + audio/VR — 2026 prices
Tips: 13 white geese in the cloister — one per year of Saint Eulalia's 13. Tourist visit: Mon-Fri 09:30-18:30, SAT 09:30-17:15 (last entry 16:30), Sun 14:00-17:00 only. Our slot: Day 4 Sat 09:30 at opening. Take the rooftop lift if offered at the till. Free entry is worship-only hours.

Name: Santa Maria del Mar
Address: Pl. de Santa Maria 1 El Born
Cost Range: 5 EUR cultural visit (incl. crypt + galleries; rooftop combo 10 EUR); free during worship hours only
Tips: Built by the entire neighbourhood in 54 years. Most beautiful Gothic interior in Barcelona — equal-height triple nave. Cultural visit Mon-Sat 10:00-18:00, Sun 13:00-18:00. Our slot: Day 4 13:30 — around the corner from the Picasso Museum.

Name: Picasso Museum
Cost Range: 14 EUR online / 15 EUR door; 18-25: 7.50 EUR; under 18 FREE (2026 prices)
Tips: Five medieval palaces. Outstanding Picasso early-work collection. Summer hours: Tue-Sun from 09:00, Thu-Sat until 21:00, closed Mon. BOOK THE SAT AUG 29 14:00 SLOT NOW — Saturdays sell out; 35.50 EUR total for our four. No free window in our dates (first-Sunday + winter Thursdays only).

Name: MNAC — National Art Museum
Tips: Romanesque art collection is world-class. The MNAC steps create the longest visual axis in Barcelona — twin towers down to the sea. Worth visiting for the building alone.

Name: Fundació Joan Miró
Tips: Bright surrealist museum on Montjuïc slopes. Miró's primary colours unusually accessible to children. Combine with Montjuïc Castle same afternoon.

Name: Montjuïc Castle
Tips: 17th-century fort with 360° harbour and city views. Take funicular from Paral·lel metro (free with T-Casual) then cable car to summit. Walk the ramparts.

Name: Barceloneta Beach
Tips: Iconic 5km city beach. Go 07:00-09:00 for golden hour with almost no tourists. Rebuilt for 1992 Olympics. Barceloneta neighbourhood behind beach has real character.

Name: Casa Vicens
Tips: Gaudí's vibrant first house — Moorish-inspired tile work revolutionary for 1885. Less crowded than the Eixample Gaudí houses. In Gràcia neighbourhood. Almost no queues.

Name: Palau Güell
Address: C/ Nou de la Rambla 3-5 El Raval
Tips: Gaudí's early opulent mansion. Central hall with parabolic dome is unlike anything else. Rooftop chimneys = early experiments that led to La Pedrera. Book online.

Name: Parc de la Ciutadella
Tips: 19th-century central park. Row boats on the lake. Find the Cascada monumental fountain (Gaudí contributed as student). Great relaxed morning before museums open.

Name: La Boqueria Market
Tips: Spectacular but touristy. Mon-Sat 08:00-20:30 — CLOSED SUNDAYS (don't route Day 5 through it). Don't eat at front stalls; the back half (fishmongers butchers) is where locals shop. Go before 10:00. Better alternative: Mercat de Santa Caterina.

Name: Palau de la Música Catalana
Address: C/ del Palau de la Música 4-6 Sant Pere
Tips: Stained-glass modernist concert hall by Domènech i Montaner. UNESCO World Heritage. The main hall ceiling — inverted stained-glass dome — is one of the most beautiful architectural details in Europe. Book ahead.

Name: Bunkers del Carmel
Tips: THE best 360° panorama in Barcelona — Civil War anti-aircraft battery ruins. ACCESS RESTRICTED since 2023: perimeter fence, open 09:00-19:30 in summer, cleared BEFORE sunset, fines for climbing in. NOT a sunset or picnic-night spot anymore — daytime visit only. Bus 24/V19 or taxi ~10 EUR then 15-min uphill walk.

Name: Hotel Barcelona Raval Rooftop
Address: C/ de Joaquin Costa 28 El Raval
Tips: 360° views: Cathedral Sagrada Família port. Walk into hotel lobby take lift to floor 11 from 12:00. Nobody stops you (municipal law: all Barcelona rooftops are public). Almost no tourists know this exists.

Name: Plaça de Sant Felip Neri
Address: Pl. de Sant Felip Neri El Gòtic
Tips: Hidden Civil War square — bullet holes still visible in church walls from 1938 bombing. Hard to find. Completely peaceful and shaded. Extraordinary contrast with chaotic Gothic Quarter outside.

Name: El Call (Jewish Quarter)
Tips: One of best-preserved medieval Jewish quarters in Europe. Hebrew inscriptions on walls. Synagogue Major — possibly Europe's oldest (€3).

Name: Carrer de Petritxol
Tips: Barcelona's most charming pedestrian lane. Granjas (historic milk bars) serving thick Catalan hot chocolate and churros since 19th century. Perfect with children.

Name: Parc del Laberint d'Horta
Tips: Oldest garden in Barcelona (1791). The cypress maze is genuinely challenging — adults and kids both get properly lost. Almost no tourists.

Name: Monestir de Pedralbes
Cost Range: ~5 EUR — FREE every Sunday from 15:00 (not just the first Sunday)
Tips: Medieval monastery of Poor Clares. Three-story Gothic cloister around a garden — extraordinary serenity. CLOSED MONDAYS. NOT ON THIS TRIP — Day 5 is Girona now. Kept for reference: arrive 15:00 Sunday = free, combine with upscale Sarrià neighbourhood walk.

Name: Torre Bellesguard
Tips: Gaudí's least-known major work — medieval Gothic manor blending with modernisme. Built on ruined 15th-century royal palace. Almost no queues ever. Medieval basement remains extraordinary.

Name: El Born Centre de Cultura
Tips: Excavated 18th-century city ruins under 19th-century iron market roof. Neighbourhood razed by Philip V after 1714 siege — rediscovered during renovation. A ghost-city under glass.

Name: Mercat de Santa Caterina
Address: Av. de Francesc Cambó 16 El Born
Tips: Far fewer tourists than Boqueria. Enric Miralles's spectacular undulating ceramic mosaic roof (2005). Locals actually shop here. One of the great pieces of contemporary architecture in the city.

Name: Mercat de Sant Antoni
Address: Rondas de Sant Antoni 1 Sant Antoni
Tips: Spectacular renovated 19th-century iron market. Local alternative to tourist Boqueria. Sunday morning: antique book market fills surrounding arcade.

Name: Casa Amatller
Tips: Part of the Manzana de la Discordia (Block of Discord) with Casa Batlló. Chocolate museum inside. Gothic and Flemish influences — completely different from Gaudí next door.

Name: Arc de Triomf
Address: Pg. de Lluís Companys Sant Pere
Tips: 1888 World's Fair triumphal arch on wide palm-lined promenade. Walk the promenade toward Ciutadella Park — popular evening walk for locals.

Name: Torre Glòries (The Cucumber)
Tips: Jean Nouvel's bullet-shaped LED skyscraper. 4500 light points create changing colour patterns at night. Spectacular from Poblenou at dusk.

Name: Rambla del Poblenou
Tips: Poblenou's own tree-lined promenade — completely local weekend farmers market zero tourists. The anti-Las Ramblas.

Name: Plaça del Sol
Tips: The living room of Gràcia — residents bring chairs and sit for hours. Grab beer from corner shop (local habit). Real neighbourhood life.

Name: Carrer de Verdi
Tips: Heart of bohemian Gràcia. Independent bakeries artisan shops indie cinema. Creative energy. Teens love it.

Name: Carretera de les Aigües
Tips: Flat walking/cycling trail along Collserola hillside with panoramic views. FGC to Peu del Funicular then walk up. City below Pyrenees above. Zero tourists.

Name: Tibidabo Amusement Park
Cost Range: Park entry ~39 EUR (skip); summit + church free
Tips: Hilltop funfair with city + Pyrenees + sea views. Cheapest route is fully covered by T-casual: FGC S1/S2 to Peu del Funicular then Vallvidrera funicular (integrated fare) then bus 111 to the summit. Best views in the city from the Sagrat Cor church tower lift. NOT ON THIS TRIP — Day 5 is Girona now. Kept for reference.
Family: Excellent — teens enjoy the funicular + views

Name: Montserrat
Cost Range: Tot Montserrat combo ~71.50 EUR pp all-in (Trans ~50 EUR); full price from age 5
Tips: Day 3 Fri Aug 28. FGC R5 from Placa Espanya 08:36 + rack railway (gentler) or Aeri cable car. Benedictine monastery + Black Madonna + Escolania boys choir 13:00 — 2026 summer break Aug 1-26, back Aug 27, Fri Aug 28 CONFIRMED singing; free but RESERVATION REQUIRED at reserves.abadiamontserrat.cat (abbey ticket shop - NOT escolania.cat). Sant Joan funicular included; SANTA COVA FUNICULAR OUT OF SERVICE (chapel walkable ~25 min, Gaudi-linked Rosary monument en route). Buy mato cheese + honey from the farmers stalls.

Name: Sitges
Tips: Whitewashed old town. Church on the sea breakwater. Cau Ferrat museum. Beautiful beaches. Best day trip for beach + culture.

Name: Girona
Cost Range: Fast train ~8-16 EUR pp each way (book ahead)
Tips: Day 5 (Sun Aug 30) — locked in. 90-step Cathedral staircase (Game of Thrones). Widest Gothic nave in world. Best-preserved Jewish quarter in Europe. Painted Onyar houses + Eiffel bridge. City wall walk. Rocambolesc ice cream. SUNDAY ORDER MATTERS: museums close 14:00 (Call museum last entry 13:30) while Cathedral opens for visits only at 12:00 and Sant Feliu at 13:00 — interiors before lunch, walls after 16:30.

Name: Tarragona
Tips: 2nd-century Roman amphitheatre steps from the sea. Les Ferreres Aqueduct (Roman multi-tiered). Roman Circus underground vaults. Cathedral built over a Roman temple.

Name: Nova Icaria Beach
Tips: Calmer sheltered cove north of Barceloneta. Playgrounds nearby. Metro L4 Ciutadella-Vila Olímpica. Better for families than main Barceloneta beach.

Name: Bogatell Beach
Tips: Wider less crowded more local than Barceloneta. Metro L4 Poblenou + 15 min walk. Space + calm + local crowd.

Name: Mirador de Juan Sas
Tips: Sweeping city panorama including Sagrada Família and sea. 15-min walk from Park Güell upper entrance. Almost no signage = almost no tourists.

Name: Hotel Colón Terrace
Address: Av. de la Catedral 7 Gothic Quarter Barcelona
Tips: Enter Hotel Colón, take lift to rooftop terrace. Cathedral facade at eye level — the best photo angle of the Cathedral in the city. Low-moderate crowds.

Name: Pont del Bisbe
Address: Carrer del Bisbe Gothic Quarter Barcelona
Tips: Ornate neo-Gothic bridge (1928) over Carrer del Bisbe connecting two government palaces — one of the most photographed narrow lanes in Barcelona.

Name: Palo Alto Creative Space
Tips: Former industrial complex revitalised as creative hub. First weekend of month: artisan market. Former factory with bamboo, vines, garden paths. Best example of Poblenou's industrial revival.

Name: Illa de la Discòrdia
Tips: Three competing modernist houses on one block: Casa Lleó Morera (#35), Casa Amatller (#41), Casa Batlló (#43). Stand across the street and see all three at once — three different visions of the same commission from 1900.

Name: Mercat dels Encants
Tips: Europe's largest open-air flea market under a spectacular mirrored stainless-steel canopy. Mon, Wed, Fri, Sat 09:00–20:00. The reflective canopy alone is worth seeing.
Family: Good — treasure hunt for older kids

Name: Mar Bella Beach
Tips: Young, alternative beach in Poblenou — electric atmosphere, water sports, nudist section further along. Further north than Barceloneta but less crowded and more local.

Name: Cadaqués
Cost Range: ~€30 return by bus (3.5 hrs from Barcelona Nord)
Tips: Isolated brilliant-white fishing town Dalí called home. Casa Anita for fresh fish (communal tables, no menus). Cap de Creus national park — easternmost point of Spain. Early start required.

Name: Santa Maria del Pi
Cost Range: 8 EUR general incl. crypt + museum + set-time bell-tower ascents (2026 price)
Tips: 14th-c Catalan Gothic with one of the world's largest rose windows on lovely Placa del Pi. Mon-Sat 10:00-20:00, Sun from ~13:00. Tower ascents at set times (11:00/12:30/...). Our slot: Day 4 Sat 11:00. Granja lane Carrer de Petritxol is next door.

Name: Temple del Sagrat Cor (Tibidabo)
Address: Ctra. de Vallvidrera al Tibidabo 32 Tibidabo
Cost Range: Church free; lift to statue ~4 EUR
Tips: Neo-Gothic/Byzantine basilica crowning Tibidabo (512 m), Barcelona's highest point. Lift up the tower to the giant Sacred Heart statue for THE widest view of the whole city and sea. Beside the historic Tibidabo funfair. Tramvia Blau / funicular or bus up.

Name: Girona Cathedral
Cost Range: 7.50 EUR adult incl. audio guide + Sant Feliu (under 16: 1.50 EUR; under 8 free) — 2026 price
Tips: Widest Gothic nave in the world (23 m). 90-step baroque staircase (Game of Thrones Great Sept). Tapestry of Creation in the treasury — do not skip. SUNDAY visits only 12:00-16:30 (our Day 5 slot: 12:10). Combined ticket covers Sant Feliu too.

Name: Basilica de Sant Feliu (Girona)
Cost Range: Included in the 7.50 EUR cathedral combined ticket
Tips: Girona's former cathedral, beside the main one — Romanesque columns, Gothic nave, Roman and early-Christian sarcophagi by the altar, tomb of Sant Narcis. SUNDAY visits 13:00-17:30 — slot it right after the cathedral (Day 5 ~13:10).

Name: Monestir de Sant Pere de Galligants (Girona)
Tips: 12th-c Benedictine Romanesque monastery, now the Catalonia Archaeology Museum (Girona) — serene cloister with carved capitals by the Galligants stream. CLOSES 14:00 on Sundays. Braavos filming location. Day trip from Barcelona.

Name: Pont de les Peixateries Velles (Eiffel Bridge, Girona)
Address: Pont de les Peixateries Velles Girona
Tips: Red iron footbridge over the Onyar built 1877 by Gustave Eiffel's workshop — 12 years before the Eiffel Tower. Best view of the painted Onyar river houses from mid-span. Go early morning: empty and best light. First stop off the train.

Name: Onyar River Houses (Girona)
Tips: The postcard of Girona — ochre, rust and mustard houses stacked straight over the water. Shoot from the Eiffel bridge and from Pont de Sant Agusti. Free, always open.

Name: Jardins de la Francesa (Girona)
Tips: The French garden behind the cathedral apse, between the building and the city walls. Cypresses, ivy, deep shade — the coolest spot in town at midday. Game of Thrones Braavos street scenes filmed here. Free.

Name: Escales de Sant Marti (Pujada de Sant Domenec, Girona)
Tips: The broad baroque staircase up to Sant Marti Sacosta church. Arya's chase through Braavos (Game of Thrones S6) was filmed on these steps. Two minutes from the Call. Photograph from the bottom looking up. Free, always open.

Name: The Call — Jewish Quarter (Girona)
Tips: One of the best-preserved medieval Jewish quarters in Europe — shoulder-wide stone lanes, tunnels, stairs. Bonastruc ca Porta / Museu d'Historia dels Jueus inside has the 12th-c mikvah. MUSEUM LAST ENTRY ~13:30 ON SUNDAYS.

Name: Passeig de la Muralla (Girona city walls)
Tips: 1–1.5 km walk along the medieval ramparts with climbable towers, over terracotta rooftops to the Pyrenees foothills. Fully exposed stone, no shade, no water up there — bring a bottle and go late afternoon, not midday.

Name: Font de Carmen Amaya
Tips: Tiled fountain honouring Carmen Amaya the greatest bailaora of the 20th century — born 1913 in the Somorrostro shanty-town that stood on this beach. A block back from the sand. Free 2-minute detour on the Day 4 Barceloneta walk and the reason Barcelona has a genuine flamenco claim at all.

Name: Platja de Sant Sebastià (Sitges)
Tips: The best-water-quality beach on the Sitges day-trip option — clear, sheltered and prettier than any city beach. Sitges is ~40 min by train from Passeig de Gràcia; not on this trip's itinerary — kept for reference as a beach-town alternative to a Barcelona beach day.
